verdict.rationale: The only evidence that AnythingLLM itself handles voice is a community comment saying it supports TTS/STT, enough to build a voice chatbot. That implies spoken replies and voice input, but no first-party docs describe voice notes, read-aloud replies or live voice conversation in chat. The meeting-transcription feature is a related but separate capability and is not credited here. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of voice input/dictation in chat, spoken-reply (TTS) settings, live two-way voice conversation mode, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, I can interact by voice — voice notes get transcribed, replies can be spoken, or live voice conversations are supported

citations.quote: it supports embedding models, vector databases, and TTS/STT, everything needed to build a fully functioning voice chatbot
